newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electric futures finish mixed, mirror cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electric futures finish mixed, mirror cash.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures settled mixed Monday, mirroring the divergent movement of cash prices in the Northwest and Southwest markets after the complex's gain last week, industry sources said.
"I see COB (California-Oregon Border) topped out...PV (Palo Verde) still looks strong," said a Houston trader.
Physical power prices in the Northwest were pressured by Bonneville Power Administration's price decrease for energy for next-day delivery, traders said.

Spot electricity values in the Southwest were support by unplanned outages of a couple of coal-fired unit outages and firm cooling demand due to hot, dry weather in the southern California and much of Arizona, they added.

Some participants noted that several Southwest utilities were forced to buy power in the spot market today because they oversold their generation for October, and needed to cover their higher-than-expected native load.
November COB futures settled down 20 cents at $17.95 a megawatt hour (MWh) below the $18.00 psychological support after hitting a session high of $18.40.
December COB finished down 16 cents at $19.08, and January 1997 COB ended down five cents at $18.00.
November PV futures closed at $17.25 a MWh, unchanged from Friday's settled.
December PV ended up 10 cents at $17.80 after briefly touching $17.90.
The latest forecasts indicated the entire western U.S. would expericence above to much-above normal autumn temperatures next week.
NYMEX estimated 95 COB and 31 PV contracts changed hands Monday.
